name: Connecticut
summary: A white baroque shield with three grapevines on an azure field, above a ribbon with the motto 'Qui Transtulit Sustinet' (He who transplanted still sustains).
origin: The grapevines come from the seal of the Saybrook Colony and appear in Connecticut's seal from 1639. The flag was adopted by the General Assembly on 3 June 1897, based on a 1895 proposal by the Daughters of the American Revolution.

symbols.name: Three grapevines
symbols.description: Three fruiting vines on the shield.
symbols.meaning: The first three colonial settlements: Hartford, Windsor and Wethersfield; also the colonists 'transplanted' from England.

symbols.name: Motto
symbols.meaning: He who transplanted still sustains, a reference to Psalm 80.

facts: Its motto has been used since colonial times.
The flag is often grouped among the 'seals on a bedsheet' criticised by vexillologists.
Connecticut is nicknamed the Constitution State.
clues: A white shield with three grapevines on blue, with a Latin motto.
Its vines are said to be three early settlements.
Its motto means 'He who transplanted still sustains'.
